column4: text   (the speaker is the subtitle caption; profile picks the voice and its processing)
There it is. Hollowmere. Nobody has set foot here since the flood of sixty-two.
Ten minutes of footage, then we are gone. I am not staying here after dark.
What was that? Something hit us! The engine is smashed, and the lamp is gone with it.
Welcome, children. My choir is short of voices.
Did you hear that? Okay. Okay. I need fuel, a toolbox, and a lantern for the fog. Search the village. And stay together.
Can you hear me? Check the houses and the sheds. The ferryman kept everything out here.
That's fuel! It's heavy, you won't be able to run with it. Bring it back to the boat.
The ferryman's toolbox! Bring it back to me.
A lantern. Good. We'll need it to find our way through the fog.
Tank's full.
Okay. I can work with these.
Lamp's lit.
That's one. Two more to go.
One more. Just one more, and we're leaving.
He's coming for you! Run! Get out of his sight!
Lose him between the houses! He can't chase what he can't see or hear!
Hide in the old wardrobes. He only looks inside if he saw you go in.
He drowned you. The water gave you back... but it will not do that forever.
No. No, no, no. They're gone. Keep moving. Please, keep moving.
The engine's running! Everybody get to the boat! We're getting out of here!
No one leaves my parish.
No! Let go of me! Help me! Help me!
He has taken her to the chapel, to sing with the others.
Free his choir, and the chapel doors will open. Find their things. Lay them on their graves.
That was Agnes Pell's. She sang so sweetly. Her grave is by the chapel.
That belonged to Thomas Hale. He tried to break the doors down.
Ruth Ellery's. She held my hand when the water came in.
Elias Grey's. He played the organ until the very end.
Margaret Lowe's. She was my teacher.
I can stop singing now. Thank you.
The doors. I can finally leave.
So cold. For so long. Thank you, child.
The music has stopped. At last.
Tell Lily... tell her I am sorry.
It's so cold in here. He keeps making me sing. Please hurry.
There are others in here with me. Under the water. Their eyes are open.
You steal my singers? Then you will sing in their place.
The chapel doors are open. Mara is inside. Take his bell, and he will let her go.
That. Is. Mine.
I can move! I'm out! I'm running to the boat. Bring that bell, and don't stop!
He can hear his bell. Wherever it goes, he follows. Pass it on if he gets close.
The bell's aboard! Everybody, get in the boat!
Hold on to something!
You will come back. They always come back to Hollowmere.
You found my music box. Now I can go home too. Goodbye.
Don't come back. Please. Don't ever come back.
Sing, children. Sing for me, forever.
My music box! Please, take it to the jetty steps. That is where I fell.
Thank you. I can hear my song again.
I can hear your heart.
Run, little lamb. Run.
There is room in the choir for you.
Sing for me.
The water remembers every name.
Why do you hide from your shepherd?
Come out, child. The water is warm.
Hide, then. I have all night.
You cannot hide from the bell.
Another voice for my choir.
Hush now. Sing.
That is not yours to take.
I am here.
There you are.
Behind you.
Don't turn around.
He sees you.
Join us.
Every part is in. Now prime the engine and pull the cord as the needle crosses the green. Every miss carries across the water.
Too early! He heard that!
She is running!
Listen. Then sing it back to me.
No. Not like that. Again.
The bell is chained with three locks. Turn each dial until it hums hot, then set it. Slowly.
That is all three. The bell is loose. Take it, and he will come.
I hear you.
Hush.
Hush now. He is listening.
